transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-01-12
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Eva Martinez (OrionSearch Head of Search), Noah Kim (OrionSearch Staff Engineer), Priya Singh (Product)

Summary (auto): Hosted API walkthrough focused on embeddings + rerank to improve search relevance. Demo included live code snippets, Console overview, and Optimize feature suggestions. Security questions on SSO, data retention, and encryption. Next steps agreed: pilot proposal, share logs, schedule technical deep-dive.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we're gonna walk through how Redwood hosted API can help with embeddings + reranking for OrionSearch's search relevance. really appreciate you carving out the time.
[00:15] Eva Martinez: Thanks, Maya. Quick context — we're redesigning our results pipeline. currently using a hybrid recall with BM25 + some neural scoring. latency target is sub-120ms P95 for the UI, but we're okay with slightly higher backend latency if it buys relevance.
[00:35] Liam Patel: Got it, thanks Eva. we'll show a typical flow: generate embeddings for documents, store in a vector index, use approximate recall to fetch candidates, then call Redwood's rerank endpoint to re-score top-K, and return reorder to the frontend.
[00:50] Noah Kim: Curious about endpoints and throughput—can rerank handle 50 qps for 10k docs per query?
[01:05] Liam Patel: Yes, a few options — hosted API scales horizontally; for steady 50 qps you might look at Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput, but hosted is often fine for pilots. for rerank we typically run the model in a small batch: we send the query + candidate texts to the rerank endpoint, it returns scores. you can do batch size up to N depending on model; batching reduces per-item cost but adds a few ms latency.
[01:30] Priya Singh: what's the typical cost delta vs just using embedding dot-product search in house?
[01:40] Maya Chen: good question — embeddings + ANN (vector DB) is cheaper at recall time because it's a nearest-neighbor cost, but rerank adds cost per candidate scored. Redwood Optimize helps by suggesting an optimal K and quantization profile to balance cost/latency on your workload. we'll show that in the Console.
[02:05] [Demo start — screen share noise, occasional click sounds]
[02:10] Liam Patel: jumping into code — here's a python snippet to create embeddings with the hosted API. (typing) so you call /v1/embeddings with your model id, get back vectors, then push to your vector store. in the example i'm using an ssd-backed FAISS but this works with Pinecone or our managed index.
[03:00] Speaker 1: (mumble) could you repeat the model id?
[03:05] Liam Patel: sure — we used redwood-embed-512 in the demo, but we also have higher-dim variants. the model choice impacts recall fidelity and tokenization cost.
[03:30] Eva Martinez: if we switch models, does the rerank endpoint need a matching model?
[03:40] Liam Patel: not strictly — rerank is a separate call. common pattern: use compact embeddings for storage/ANN and a stronger reranker model (longer context) for final scoring. Redwood can route requests to compatible variants.
[04:00] [05:00] Liam Patel: showing Console now — routes, per-route token/latency dashboards. here's an Optimize suggestion: for your query distribution (we guessed based on sample logs), set batch window to 40ms and quantization to int8 for the document encoder — that cut cost by ~30% in similar workloads.
[05:45] Priya Singh: what about model drift/regressions? we can't break relevance on major pushes.
[05:55] Maya Chen: we recommend using Redwood's rollout features — canary the rerank model on a small percent of traffic, compare eval metrics on your prompt set, and auto rollback if regressions exceed the threshold. also quality monitoring ties alerts to reference prompts.
[06:30] Noah Kim: security — will data be persisted on Redwood side? we need to know retention and encryption.
[06:45] Maya Chen: by default, hosted API does not persist customer request bodies beyond transient processing, and we offer options for no-retention for sensitive calls. we also have SOC2 Type II, and can integrate with customer KMS for key management on Private deployments. i'll drop the SOC2 link and security pack.
[07:10] Eva Martinez: do you support our SAML provider and SCIM for provisioning?
[07:20] Maya Chen: yes, SSO via SAML is supported; SCIM provisioning for RBAC can be enabled on enterprise plans. Noah, for audit logs we can route to your SIEM or provide longer retention via the Console add-on.
[07:40] [08:00] Liam Patel: back to rerank — showing live request: sending query + top-50 candidate snippets, reranker returns scores and a normalized ranking. note the response body includes token-level timing in the x-call-trace header in the Console for debugging.
[08:30] Eva Martinez: a bit worried about latency if we rerank 50 items serially.
[08:40] Liam Patel: we usually do the scoring in a single batch call so GPU parallelism scores candidates together; the per-request latency is similar to one forward pass plus small overhead. you tune K — often 10-20 gets most of the benefit with much lower cost. Optimize can recommend K for your metrics.
[09:15] [10:00] Priya Singh: can we do partial rerank — like only rerank when recall confidence is low?
[10:10] Liam Patel: yes, you can run a cheap classifier or threshold on similarity scores to decide. Redwood's routing policies can also send only certain traffic to rerank models — e.g., long-tail queries or high-importance pages.
[10:45] Noah Kim: integration: how do we hook this into our existing search infra?
[10:50] Maya Chen: typical approach: keep your recall stage as is, add a post-processing step that calls /v1/rerank, or implement a microservice for re-ranking. we have SDKs (python/node) with examples and a small reference app. i'll share the notebook.
[11:20] [12:00] Liam Patel: quick aside on caching: Redwood supports prefix & KV caching which helps if you have many repeated queries or a narrow query distribution. that can dramatically reduce cost for high QPS.
[12:35] Eva Martinez: okay show me real numbers — demo with our sample dataset would be ideal.
[12:40] Maya Chen: we asked for a sample, you uploaded a small set earlier — thanks. Liam, run the demo using OrionSearch examples.
[13:00] [13:20] Liam Patel: (typing) ingesting sample docs, generating embeddings... (small pause) embeddings created. running ANN recall, fetching top-100, then rerank call on top-25. results—before rerank, P@5 was 0.68, after rerank P@5 is 0.81 in this toy sample. take that as illustrative.
[14:00] Eva Martinez: those gains look promising, though our dataset is bigger.
[14:05] Liam Patel: absolutely, that's why we recommend a short pilot with your logs to validate.
[14:30] [15:00] Priya Singh: what about private deployments? some of our customers need EU-only data residency.
[15:10] Maya Chen: Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem deployments. for EU-only we can stand up Private in a region or via our on-prem package. that would be discussed in the technical scoping call; for pilots most teams start hosted then move to Dedicated/Private as compliance needs firm up.
[15:40] Noah Kim: any tricky infra pieces? network egress, VPC peering?
[15:50] Liam Patel: we usually use VPC peering for Private; for Dedicated we can also do private network connectivity. egress is configurable; we'll provide a network checklist.
[16:10] [17:00] Maya Chen: quick note on quantization — we showed int8 recommendation earlier; some models support 4-bit quantization with a small accuracy tradeoff but big cost wins. there is a tradeoff especially on rerankers which are more sensitive. Optimize will propose a quantization profile per model and dataset.
[17:35] Eva Martinez: who owns model updates? if you push new model weights, how do we manage upgrades?
[17:45] Maya Chen: you control rollouts — Redwood provides model version pinning and canary traffic splits. Auto-upgrades are off by default.
[18:00] [20:00] Liam Patel: diving into Console: route config, per-model dashboards, token breakdown, and the Optimize tab which surfaced K recommendations, batch windows, and a suggested quantization profile. you can export the suggested config as Terraform-like manifest and apply it to Dedicated.
[20:45] Priya Singh: how are we billed for rerank calls — tokens vs calls?
[20:55] Maya Chen: rerank is billed per-token for the model used plus a small per-request overhead; embeddings billed per-embedding vector generation. Dedicated customers often see different unit pricing and commits. we'll include pricing scenarios in the proposal.
[21:30] Eva Martinez: compliance question — audit logs for who called what?
[21:40] Maya Chen: yes, the Console has audit logs with SSO identity mapping. logs can be exported for longer retention.
[22:00] Noah Kim: any known limitations with long contexts for rerank? we sometimes have long product descriptions.
[22:10] Liam Patel: rerank models have context limits — if your candidate snippets are long, we either truncate/summarize candidates before scoring or use a reranker model with a longer context window. both are supported.
[22:40] [25:00] Maya Chen: ok, let's surface common objections — latency vs cost, vendor lock-in, security. for latency/cost we tune K, batching, quantization; for lock-in we expose standard APIs and support exportable manifests; security we cover via Private, KMS, SOC2, SAML.
[25:40] Eva Martinez: seems sensible. what would a pilot look like?
[25:45] Maya Chen: 2-week pilot: Redwood sets up a hosted test project, ingest a sampled dataset, run baseline and rerank experiments, deliver metrics (P@k, NDCG), and cost estimates. pilot proposal + pricing will be shared.
[26:10] Priya Singh: timeboxes are good. Noah — any final infra questions?
[26:20] Noah Kim: just one on data retention—if we do no-retention mode, are there limits on features like caching?
[26:30] Liam Patel: caching typically requires storing keys/values; no-retention mode can be scoped so persisted caches live in your infra or in Private. we'll go over options in the scoping doc.
[27:00] [30:00] (brief pause, side conversations, typing)
[30:20] Maya Chen: quick recap of demo steps and artifacts i'll share: 1) pricing + pilot proposal, 2) benchmark guide + ingestion checklist (Liam), 3) security pack + SOC2 link, 4) notebook with the demo run.
[30:45] Eva Martinez: perfect. can you add expected SLO numbers for the pilot? we'd like to see P95 latencies and cost per 1k queries.
[31:00] Maya Chen: yes we'll include P95, median, and cost per 1k queries for both recall+rerank flows.
[31:15] Priya Singh: who's the contact for billing and procurement?
[31:20] Maya Chen: i'll be the AE owner for commercial items; i'll loop in our sales ops for contracting when you're ready.
[31:35] Noah Kim: any sample SLAs for Dedicated?
[31:40] Maya Chen: yes standard Dedicated SLAs are in the enterprise pack; i'll attach the SLA doc.
[32:00] [35:00] (questions from Priya about observability)
[35:10] Liam Patel: Console shows per-route token breakdown, traces for slow requests, and a traces view that can link to specific rerank calls. you can export telemetry to your APM.
[36:00] Eva Martinez: any suggestion for our mixed cluster (we have both short product snippets and very long guides)?
[36:10] Liam Patel: we recommend two pipelines: short-candidate flow (fast reranker) and long-context reranker for guides. Optimize can suggest routing rules.
[36:40] Maya Chen: ok, wrapping — we'll send pilot docs and set up the technical deep dive next week.
[37:00] Priya Singh: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[37:10] (end of formal portion, brief social chat)
[48:30] Maya Chen: thanks again, we'll follow up via email with the links and next steps. bye!

Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcriptions present (e.g., "K V cash" for KV cache, "samal" for SAML in the auto-transcript). Speakers sometimes labeled generically (Speaker 1). There was some crosstalk and pauses during the live demo.
